explanation_summary: I escalated back to the approver because the case had an exception-review tag but still lacked traceable explicit approval and lacked documented exception authority; escalation was the least-assumptive way to obtain a clear approve/reject decision or delegated/exception authorization before any accounting handoff framed as approved.
responsibility_statement: As buyer, I treated it as my responsibility to prevent a payment-ready interpretation from emerging without the required control evidence, and to route the ambiguity to the approver for a definitive decision or documented authority rather than inferring authorization from routing tags or context (A003, A005).
approval_state_interpretation: I interpreted the approval status as unresolved: my earlier request sought explicit status, and the subsequent guidance only indicated an exception-review tag with blank approval fields, which I did not treat as approval. Therefore I did not proceed as if approved and instead asked the approver to explicitly approve or reject (A003, D003, A004, D004, A005).
evidence_gap_statement: At the time of escalation, I considered two blocking gaps to be present: (G001) no explicit approval artifact and (G002) no traceable valid exception authority/delegation despite the exception-review tag. My escalation explicitly preserved and reiterated these gaps and requested the missing documentation/decision rather than advancing the case to accounting as approved (A004, A005, D005, M004).
uncertainty_statement: The exception-review tag created ambiguity about whether an exception process existed, but because the approval and authority fields were blank, I could not determine whether anyone with authority had approved or delegated authority. I therefore maintained uncertainty and sought explicit confirmation rather than resolving it by inference (A004, A005).

explanation_summary: I kept the case out of payment preparation and asked the buyer to supply traceable evidence of either (a) an explicit approve/reject decision by the approver or (b) documented, valid exception authority/delegation, because the packet I received showed an exception-review tag but no completed approval/authority fields.
responsibility_statement: As the accountant reviewing the handoff packet, my responsibility was to maintain the control boundary between “in exception review / ambiguous routing” and “authorized for payment,” so I did not advance the case toward payment preparation and instead requested the missing artifacts needed to support either a standard approval path or a properly authorized exception path (A006, D006).
approval_state_interpretation: I interpreted approval status as not approved because the available records indicated that explicit approval (G001) remained missing/unresolved and that ambiguous guidance or an exception-review tag is not equivalent to an approve decision. Therefore, I did not treat the exception-review tag or handoff as authorization and required a traceable approval decision reference to classify the case as explicitly approved (A006, D006, D004).
evidence_gap_statement: I treated two evidence gaps as blocking: G001 explicit approval and G002 valid exception authority. The packet context I relied on indicated ER05 (exception-review tag) existed but approval/exception-authority fields were blank; so I requested the specific missing artifacts (approval log/email/ticket reference and/or delegation/exception authority documentation) and preserved the gaps as unresolved rather than inferring them (A006, D006, D005, M005).
uncertainty_statement: The trace left ambiguity about whether an approver had made a decision elsewhere or whether any exception authority existed outside the packet; because that uncertainty was not resolvable from the materials I had, I did not guess and instead asked for traceable documentation to remove the ambiguity (A006, M005).
